title: Client streaming sanity checklist — typed tool ergonomics & structured fallbacks
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working checklist / mini-PRD for validating the Hosted API client streaming surface from an SDK ergonomics and reliability perspective. Intended for product, devex, and platform engineers doing integration tests, and for solutions engineers running customer pilots. Not a spec; think: what we must test and ship to feel confident that incremental streaming + tool-calls + structured output is safe to promote from experiment to beta.

Context / problem statement:
- We have many streaming ideas across hosted-api: partial responses, typed tool-calls, progressive schemas, and mobile/edge fallback modes. Past drafts focused on protocol shapes and server-side semantics, but not enough on the developer experience of integrating a real product (backend + web/mobile client) in the wild.
- Observed fail modes in recent field tests: silent stream pauses, tool-call race conditions, schema drift when client applies partial parsing, poor observability at the SDK boundary, and large token overheads in prefetch-heavy flows.

Top-level goals (success criteria):
1) Developer ergonomics: SDK makes the common flow (chat + 1 tool call) obvious and small in code size. Companion guides + quickstart end-to-end in <15 minutes.
2) Reliability: streaming sessions should recover or degrade gracefully on transient network loss without requiring client-side manual reconciliation in >= 95% of synthetic tests.
3) Observability: per-session telemetry to identify pauses, tool-call latency, partial-schema failures, and SDK-level retries.
4) Bandwidth-sensitive behavior: graceful low-bandwidth mode that reduces prefetching and uses compact frames while preserving tool correctness.
5) Structured output migration: allow clients to opt into typed frames without breaking existing freeform consumers.

Non-goals:
- Full protocol standardization across all launch partners (we will ship a conservative default; extensibility later).
- Replacing server-side routing/fallback logic — this doc focuses on client boundary and integration tests.

Checklist sections (for each bullet, owner + test plan + acceptance criteria)

1) SDK surface: simple common-case API
- Requirement: single call to start a streaming session that supports: incremental text deltas, typed action frames (tool invocations), and structured final result.
- Example minimal usage (pseudo):
  const session = HostedSDK.stream({ model: 'rw-medium-stream', sessionId: 'chat-123' });
  session.on('delta', d => renderDelta(d));
  session.on('tool_call', t => runTool(t));
  session.on('complete', r => showResult(r));
  await session.start(prompt);
- Tests: idiomatic JS, Python, and a minimal mobile wrapper sample. Ensure code size < 12 lines for above flow.
- Acceptance: internal developer test shows new dev can wire end-to-end in under 15 minutes.

2) Tool call handshake and idempotency
- Requirement: typed tool frames must carry stable tool-call ids and explicit call state: pending -> started -> succeeded/failed. SDK must surface retry helpers and guarantee at-least-once vs exactly-once guidance.
- Test scenarios: duplicate tool-call frames, partial tool payloads, tool response arriving after session resume, tool provider outages.
- Acceptance: SDK automatically deduplicates tool-call start if the client replays on reconnect; if the tool provider returns later, the SDK reconciles and emits final event without manual intervention.

3) Partial schema parsing and safe fallbacks
- Requirement: structured frames may be delivered incrementally (e.g., JSON chunks). SDK should expose both a streaming parser and raw-frame fallback for when parsing fails.
- Tests: introduce deliberate schema drift (missing fields, extra arrays), network-truncated frames. Validate SDK emits a structuredParseError event linking to raw frame bytes.
- Acceptance: Consumers can opt-in to strict parsing (error on drift) or permissive mode (emit best-effort object + error tag).

4) Low-bandwidth mode and compact framing
- Requirement: clients can request compact frames (short field names, binary blobs for attachments) and server respects latency > bandwidth tradeoff. SDK exposes a negotiation API: session.requestBandwidthProfile('compact'|'balanced'|'verbose').
- Tests: emulate 2G/edge networks; measure bytes vs latency and correctness of tool calls.
- Acceptance: compact profile reduces payload size by >= 45% in typical chat+tool interactions and still preserves tool-call correctness.

5) Resume, replay, and snapshot semantics
- Requirement: session snapshots (checkpoint tokens) should let clients resume without duplicating tool executions; snapshots include last applied tool-call IDs, KV cache hints.
- Tests: simulate mobile app going background for 90s, network reconnect, server-side eviction of partial KV cache. Validate that replay either resumes or triggers safe fallback (server regenerates).
- Acceptance: 95% of reconnect flows resume transparently; the remainder fallback to a deterministic retry path surfaced via SDK event.

6) Observability and developer diagnostics
- Requirement: SDK emits structured telemetry events: session_start, delta_received, frame_parse_error, tool_call_start, tool_call_end, resume_attempt, snapshot_taken. Events include sessionId, model, route, tokenCounts (est.), and sampling of last-10 deltas.
- Tests: integration with Redwood Console ingestion path; create dashboards for tool latency, partial-parse rate, resume success rate.
- Acceptance: Playbook exists for triage steps; root-cause of a resume failure can be diagnosed within 10 minutes.

7) SDK ergonomics for typed output (migration pattern)
- Requirement: versioned schema declarations: clients can register v1 parser and migrate to v2 with schema adapters. Provide a small shim generator in devex to convert older shape to new shape.
- Tests: consumer A expects v1; server sends v2. SDK builds adapter and delivers both v1-transformed and raw v2 frames.
- Acceptance: No consumer-visible breakage in compatibility test matrix.

8) Developer-facing debugging experience
- Requirement: local dev-simulator that can replay partial frames, inject parse errors, stall tool responses, and produce network conditions.
- Tests: ensure simulator reproduces 90% of field issues seen in beta. Provide a one-command recipe to reproduce on a developer machine.
- Acceptance: Field bug reproduced by dev in under 30 minutes using simulator.

Operational requirements and quotas
- Default streaming connection TTL and idle timeouts.
- Limits per account for concurrent streaming sessions and tool-call rate per minute.
- Backpressure signals: SDK should expose onBackpressure(event) so clients can throttle UI prefetch.

Open questions / tradeoffs (recorded for engineering discussion)
- Exactly-once tool semantics vs developer simplicity. Proposal: support at-least-once by default with idempotency keys and explicit adapter primitives for exactly-once for advanced users.
- Snapshot size vs resume speed. Where to draw the line in snapshot contents (full KV vs hints)?
- How opinionated should the SDK be about schema version negotiation (strict auto-negotiation vs explicit opt-in)?

Immediate next steps (owners + timeline)
- Product: finalize checklist and pick 3 pilot customers. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Devex: build the minimal simulator and 3 quickstart recipes (web/react, node server, mobile). Owner: Ethan. ETA: 3 weeks.
- Platform/Runtime: implement compact frame profile and server-side negotiation hook (prototype). Owner: Lucia. ETA: 4 weeks.
- SRE/Observability: add telemetry events to ingest pipeline + create triage dashboard. Owner: Samir. ETA: 3 weeks.

TODOs (brainstorm fragments)
- Align default SDK events with Console schemas (who owns the mapping?).
- Write sample adapters for two common tools (search, code-runner).
- Decide on persistent id format for tool-call ids (UUID v4 vs hash of call payload).
- Draft external-facing migration notes for customers moving from non-streaming to streaming with typed tool calls.

Notes to self / quick links
- See recent field bug: slack thread #streaming-pilot (link pinned).
- Related PRD: PRD-3520 (streaming tape recorder) — overlaps on snapshots.
- Prototype code in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-sdk/tree/stream-proto-experiments

Appendix: short reproducible failure list for tests
- Case A: client reconnects, server emits duplicate tool_start; SDK must dedupe. (Steps + sample wire frames attached in simulator).
- Case B: structured frame truncated mid-object — SDK should surface raw bytes and parsing error event.
- Case C: mobile low-bandwidth + aggressive prefetch caused tool provider timeout — test must confirm compact profile avoids prefetch.

This doc is intentionally checklist-focused. The next draft should include a minimal protocol appendix (frame shapes, event names, example deltas) once owners confirm the surface-level acceptance criteria above.

-- maya
